terms.gloss: themselves (as object), referring to the subject
terms.grammar: pronoun, reflexive: genitive suī, dative sibi, accusative and ablative sē; the same for every gender and number
evidence: Varr. RR 3.16.38: restituunt sē ac revīvēscunt
Liv. 21.31.1: ad iter sē parāre jubet
terms.comment: The same sē as in the singular: restituunt sē, they recover (themselves). Not to be confused with “each other”, inter sē (see each other).

terms.gloss: themselves (for emphasis: they themselves, of their own accord)
evidence: Plin. NH 18.107: ipsī pānem faciēbant Quirītēs
Cic. Div. 1.74: valvae clausae sē ipsae aperuērunt (Lewis & Short, s.v. ipse, Div. 1.37.74)
terms.comment: Stresses the people or things: ipsī pānem faciēbant Quirītēs, the citizens made their bread themselves. With the reflexive it agrees with the doer or with the object: valvae clausae sē ipsae aperuērunt, the shut doors opened of themselves.

phrases.latin: quae enim sīc concaluērunt, restituunt sē ac revīvēscunt
phrases.english: For those that have been warmed in this way recover and come back to life.

phrases.latin: mōrēs quoque sē inter lūdendum simplicius dētegunt
phrases.english: Character, too, shows itself more openly in play.

phrases.latin: corpora cūrāre atque ad iter sē parāre jubet
phrases.english: He tells them to see to their bodies and get themselves ready for the march.
the shut doors opened of themselves

phrases.latin: pistōrēs Rōmae nōn fuēre ad Persicum ūsque bellum … ipsī pānem faciēbant Quirītēs, mulierumque id opus maximē erat
phrases.english: There were no bakers at Rome until the war with Perseus … the citizens made their bread themselves, and it was chiefly the women’s work.

phrases.latin: jam hortum ipsī agricolae succīdiam alteram appellant
phrases.english: And the garden the farmers themselves call their second flitch of bacon.
